dedupe_keys.name: space weather telluric activity map of canada natural resources canada

description: The Space Weather: Telluric Activity map shows zones of Canada by level of telluric activity, defined as the percentage of time in a year when variations of the geoelectric field exceed the normal level of 20 millivolts per kilometre. Natural Resources Canada publishes it because the geoelectric field, induced by the geomagnetic field, drives the currents that harm vulnerable infrastructure such as power networks and pipelines, so the key content of a space weather hazard map is where that activity is high. In the auroral zone activity is high for a quarter of the year, while in the Prairies it falls from 15 percent to a few percent; most large Canadian cities lie where it is below 10 percent. Coverage is national, as a static map (entry dated 14 March 2022). Format and access: JPEG2000 images and ZIP archives with PDF and JPG versions, in English and French, from the Open Government Portal. Licence: Open Government Licence - Canada; free. Caveats: a map image with broad zones, not gridded values or a time series. It supports hazard exposure screening of grids and pipelines. Related catalogue records are Space Weather Canada and the NRCan space weather effects chronology.
